account: The Wellington fire broke out on Sunday, 7 July 2024, at an unattended campsite just east of a Breckenridge neighborhood. Summit Daily reported on 8 July 2024 that crews were dispatched around 12:30 p.m. The officials whom it interviewed credited fuels reduction work completed 18 months earlier for the containment within hours. They did not mention the camera. Summit Daily gave the fire's size as up to a quarter-acre. CBS Colorado reported on 9 July 2024 that the fire was spotted by a Pano AI camera financially supported by Xcel Energy. The camera sits on a cell tower with a 360-degree view and submits an alert to emergency crews if it notices smoke. Firefighters said that this was the first instance in Summit County where a wildfire was caught early thanks to the camera. They said that the early notice kept it to one-eighth of an acre. Earlier alerts had been false alarms from legal campfires. Mathew Benedict of Red White and Blue Fire's Wildland Division said that a location given as latitude and longitude let crews drive straight to the fire. Otherwise they could spend up to an hour finding it. Michelle Aguayo of Xcel Energy said that the company had 28 Pano AI cameras installed. On 3 September 2024 CBS Colorado reported that Pano AI cameras had first spotted another one-eighth-acre fire near the Gold Hill Trailhead. KJCT8 reported on 5 May 2026 that Xcel Energy had more than 130 Pano AI cameras across Colorado.

purpose: Pano AI cameras scan for smoke and alert emergency crews with a location. Catching a fire near homes early was the intended use.

ratings.reason: A fire next to a residential neighborhood was kept to one-eighth of an acre. Firefighters told CBS Colorado that the camera's early notice kept it small, though the counterfactual is their judgment. Summit Daily reports that officials credit earlier fuels reduction work for the quick containment and gives the size as up to a quarter-acre.
Red White and Blue Fire received an exact location and drove straight to the fire. Benedict said that locating a wildfire can otherwise take an hour.
